modelName: A ramp of experiments, and what stops each one
modelNote: Deming and API never implement a change; they test it at increasing scale under widening conditions, and the size of the first test is set by how much is unknown and how much a failure would cost. Here the cost of failure is somebody's health, so the first test moves no money at all. Three standing rules hold across every step, and every step carries a stopping rule written down BEFORE it starts. Drawn Aug 16 2026.

legendEntries.label: Standing rule — holds in every experiment
What stops it — written down before it starts
Who is watching, with no stake in the answer
advance only if the last one held

nodes.label: 1 · CARE NEVER WAITS ON THE MONEY
nodes.note: No clinical decision is ever contingent on settlement state. The experiment runs beside care, never in front of it.

nodes.label: 2 · ADDITIVE ONLY
nodes.note: Every early experiment ADDS a service — a CHW contact, a plan conversation, a follow-up call. Nothing existing is removed, reduced or replaced until the additive version has been running long enough to show what it does. You cannot harm someone with a service they did not have before; you can very easily harm them by taking one away.

nodes.label: 3 · SILENCE IS NEUTRAL
nodes.note: A member who does not verify costs nobody anything — settlement falls back to the floor. The moment a missing signature withholds money, every ME becomes a collections agent pointed at a sick person.

nodes.label: E0 · SHADOW
nodes.note: The whole ledger runs in parallel and moves no money. Orders are posted, verifications collected, leading targets computed, the win-win statement drawn up — and everyone keeps being paid exactly as they are today. 3 to 6 months. This is where the hidden things become visible at zero risk to anyone: what a plan actually costs, who actually moves it, how often a member says the plan was not met.

nodes.label: E1 · ONE TEAM
nodes.note: One microenterprise, one condition, roughly 30 members who consent. Additive service only. Capacity payment plus an order floor. At-risk share: zero. What is being tested is whether an ME can hold an order at all — not whether incentives work.

nodes.label: E2 · VERIFICATION LIVE
nodes.note: Roughly 100 members. The member's verification now releases the remainder above the floor. Still additive, still one condition. What is being tested is whether verification is honest and uncoerced — which is why the independent sample call matters more here than anywhere else.

nodes.label: E3 · MICROCOMMUNITY + TARGET
nodes.note: Two or three MEs bound into one microcommunity around one person's plan, with a small shared upside against a leading target — and the target may not be used until it has been on a control chart long enough to show whether its movement is signal or common-cause noise.

nodes.label: E4 · OPEN ORDER BOOK
nodes.note: More than one ME may bid for an order, at risk-adjusted value. This is the last step for a reason: an open order book is where cherry-picking lives, and it must not be switched on until the risk adjustment has been tested against real plans.

nodes.label: Stops if: the shadow ledger disagrees with the real one in ways nobody can explain
nodes.note: The shadow ledger is only useful if it is believed. An unexplained divergence from the real books means the model of the money is wrong, and every later step inherits that error while attaching real consequences to it.

nodes.label: Stops if: any member is harmed · any member reports confusion about who is responsible for their care
nodes.note: Two tripwires. Harm is obvious. The second is subtler and more likely: when several MEs surround one person, responsibility can diffuse until nobody is holding it — and the person is the only one positioned to notice.

nodes.label: Stops if: any member reports being pressed to verify · verification rate climbs toward 100% (nobody is that good)
nodes.note: The verification rate climbing toward 100% is the counter-intuitive one. Nobody meets every plan; a near-perfect rate means members have learned what answer is wanted, which is the exact moment verification stops carrying information and starts laundering it.

nodes.label: Stops if: a team starts optimising the target instead of the person · declines cluster in one subgroup
nodes.note: Goal displacement, which Deming spent a career on. The tell is a target that improves while the thing it was a proxy for does not — which is only detectable if the proxy and the intent are both being watched.

nodes.label: Stops if: the sickest members wait longer for a team to take their order than anyone else
nodes.note: The cherry-picking tripwire, stated as a waiting time because that is what a member actually experiences. Risk adjustment is supposed to prevent this; this is the measurement that says whether it worked.

nodes.label: SAFETY REVIEW
nodes.note: A named person, and a small group, with authority to halt any experiment and NO financial interest in it continuing. Clinicians and members, not the co-op's finance side. They see every stopping-rule signal directly, not filtered through the people running the experiment. If this role does not exist, none of the stopping rules above are real.

nodes.label: ETHICS REVIEW
nodes.note: This is a designed experiment that changes how people's care is arranged and paid for. Whether or not it legally counts as human-subjects research, take it to a review board anyway. It is protective for members, protective for the co-op, and it is the difference between an experiment and something done to people.

nodes.label: Every step widens exactly one thing. When two things change at once and something goes wrong, you have learned nothing and you still have to stop.
nodes.note: The one-variable rule is what makes a failure informative. It costs speed and buys the ability to attribute cause, which is the whole reason for running experiments rather than launching a programme.
